claims.text: CAL FIRE's incident page for the Plaskett Fire reports that, as of September 11, 2026 at 6:31 PM, the fire (which started August 26, 2026 at 11:01 AM near Los Burros Road/Plaskett in the Los Padres National Forest, Monterey County) had burned 29,942 acres and was 83% contained, up from 79% contained the previous day; two evacuation zones have been downgraded from orders to warnings, though multiple evacuation order and warning zones remain in effect across Monterey County, and Highway 1 remains partially closed between mile marker 19 and mile marker 11.1.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 11, 2026 at 6:31 PM, the fire (which started August 8, 2026 at 8:35 PM southeast of Loma Vista in the Los Padres National Forest, Monterey County) had burned 25,420 acres and was 27% contained; evacuation orders have been downgraded in portions of Big Sur and previous shelter-in-place orders have been lifted as conditions improved, though 13 areas remain under evacuation orders and 27 under evacuation warnings across Monterey County, with crews conducting suppression, mop-up and patrol operations; no injuries or deaths were reported.

description: The Plaskett and Timber wildfires have burned roughly 55,000 combined acres along California's Big Sur coast since August 2026, forcing evacuations across two counties. The Timber Fire ignited August 8 and the larger Plaskett Fire ignited August 26 in the Los Padres National Forest near Big Sur; both remain active more than two weeks later, with CAL FIRE reporting the Plaskett Fire at about 29,900 acres and 83% contained and the Timber Fire at about 25,400 acres and 27% contained as of September 11. Evacuation orders have been downgraded in portions of Big Sur, with two Plaskett Fire zones moved from orders to warnings and previous Timber Fire shelter-in-place orders lifted, though numerous evacuation order and warning zones remain in effect across Monterey County and a stretch of Highway 1 through the Big Sur coast remains partially closed. No deaths or injuries have been reported by CAL FIRE for either fire.

impact.summary: CAL FIRE reports no deaths or injuries from either fire. As of September 11, 2026, the Plaskett Fire is 83% contained at 29,942 acres (up from 79% the day before), with two evacuation zones downgraded from orders to warnings, while the Timber Fire holds at 27% containment on 25,420 acres, with evacuation orders downgraded in portions of Big Sur and earlier shelter-in-place orders lifted. Multiple evacuation order and warning zones remain in effect across Monterey County, with warnings extending into northern San Luis Obispo County for the Plaskett Fire, and a long stretch of Highway 1 through the Big Sur coast remains partially closed to through traffic.
